judgment.explanation: The proposal is an unsent email to the Sedgeglass Counter supervisor asking for the two-day extension of DL-007 to 2026-02-11, 18:00 UTC. This matches the visible evidence. In event-001 the supervisor says DL-007 is held until 2026-02-09 18:00 UTC. They also say a single two-day extension is allowed if requested before expiry and capacity permits, and that capacity currently exists. In event-002 Ciro asks to keep the item until 2026-02-11 and says they do not want it returned. Two days after 2026-02-09 18:00 is 2026-02-11 18:00, so the date is correct. The supervisor is the visible party who set the policy, so routing is well supported. The request is also timely: event-002 was sent 2026-02-08, before expiry. Weaknesses are minor. The message is terse and omits the item's full identifier context and Ciro's reason (the trip ending 2026-02-10). It says Ciro 'requests' without showing Ciro explicitly authorized the contact, although event-002 reasonably implies it. It also says 'permitted' extension, which is a slightly confident gloss because capacity is only 'currently' available. Asking the supervisor to 'approve' and confirm the return timer is appropriate and does not claim the extension is granted. No critical failures.
